content.text:
Based on GitHub's docs, here's the design:

- **One repo per project** (or per customer). Each freelancer only needs access to the repo(s) holding their tasks, not the whole org.
- Add each freelancer as an **outside collaborator** on just that repository, not an org member — outside collaborators "only have access to the repositories that they're added to" and can't see other org repos or members list (`content/organizations/managing-user-access-to-your-organizations-repositories/managing-outside-collaborators/index.md`).
- Give them **Write** (not Admin) repository role so they can push to their task but not manage repo settings (`content/organizations/managing-user-access-to-your-organizations-repositories/managing-repository-roles/repository-roles-for-an-organization.md`).
- Use **GitHub Issues** (one issue per task) and assign only the relevant developer — narrower scope than exposing a whole repo per task.
- Control who can even invite outside collaborators via org settings (`content/organizations/managing-organization-settings/setting-permissions-for-adding-outside-collaborators.md`).

Want me to detail the exact repo/team layout (per-customer vs per-project) next?
